tex_content.html:
Lemma
[a geodesic segment has length equal to speed times elapsed parameter]

↗ lem:dc-ch3-2-1-constspeed

1. ch3:3.6Let $\gamma $ be a continuous intrinsic geodesic on a connected open set of times containing $a$ and $b$. Then the length of the arc over $[a,b]$ is the constant speed times the elapsed parameter, \[ \ell \big(\gamma |_{[a,b]}\big)=\sqrt{\langle \gamma '(a),\gamma '(a)\rangle _g}\, (b-a). \]
Proof

\sketch

The length is the integral of the intrinsic speed $\sqrt{\langle \gamma ',\gamma '\rangle _g}$ over $[a,b]$. Along a geodesic the squared speed is constant (section 1), equal to its value at $a$, so the integrand is the constant $\sqrt{\langle \gamma '(a),\gamma '(a)\rangle _g}$ and the integral is that constant times $b-a$.

□
